defect_a.name: MULTI_OUTPUT_STALENESS_MASKED
defect_a.root_cause: evaluate() took _newest() over every file produced by a stage and compared that maximum against the newest input. On a stage declaring more than one output, a fresher sibling won the max and hid an artifact genuinely older than its own input.

baseline_harm_measured.method: identical synthetic workspace driven through the real CLI on both trees
baseline_harm_measured.consequence: The baseline walked the owner past a Master Keyword List that never saw its Cerebro data and told them to build keyword intelligence on it. Stages 6, 8, 9 and 10 all consume that list.

fix.rule: each declared output PATTERN contributes its newest match; the MINIMUM is taken ACROSS patterns
deliberately_preserved: One pattern contributes one artifact; the minimum is never taken across every file on disk, so a superseded Cerebro export the owner never deleted does not mark stage 4 stale for ever.
artifact now names the OLDEST output - the file the owner must look at. Naming the fresh sibling sent them to a file that was fine.
fix.docstring_updated: The module's staleness rule read 'output mtime < input mtime', the exact ambiguity that permitted the defect. It now reads 'OLDEST output mtime < newest input mtime' and says why.

defect_b.name: QUOTE_NOT_CORRECT_QUOTING
defect_b.separable: git revert fcd6d31 removes it without touching DEFECT A
defect_b.audit_finding: A seed of 'nurse"; calc; #' printed as --seed "nurse"; calc; #", which a shell splits at the second quote.

additional_instance_found_during_fix.name: PLACEHOLDER_PRINTED_WITH_BARE_CMD_REDIRECTION_OPERATORS
additional_instance_found_during_fix.detail: <seed-keyword>, printed whenever no --seed is supplied, went out with < and > bare. Those are cmd.exe redirection operators: pasted as printed, the line does not run the command, it truncates a file named seed-keyword and reads from it. It is also the one line guaranteed to be pasted by a first-time owner.

fix.rule: anything outside [A-Za-z0-9._+=/:\-\\] forces quoting; an embedded double quote is doubled
fix.scope_honesty: The docstring claimed more than the function delivered. It now states that this makes a printed command safe to PASTE into the PowerShell and cmd.exe consoles this tool targets, and that it is NOT a shell-injection boundary and does not need to be - the seed is the owner's own text going into the owner's own shell, and the module executes nothing. This matches the audit's own conclusion.

tests.before_fix_note: 28 = the 22 baseline tests plus the 6 new DEFECT A tests, run against the baseline module.

disclosure.finding: A naive AST scan for write/exec-capable call NAMES now reports one hit that the audit's original scan did not: text.replace('"', '""') at core/pipeline_status.py:222.
disclosure.resolution: That is str.replace on a local string, not os.replace. Disambiguated by the os_attributes_used list above containing only listdir and path. It is not a filesystem call.
disclosure.why_disclosed: The audit recorded zero write/exec hits; without this note the change reads as a regression in auditability.

does_not_unlock: This is NOT the Pipeline Observer V1 from the 2026-07-31 review. That is a 10-state model with block reasons, prerequisites, freshness and source dates - a derivation layer that does not exist yet and must be scoped and tested as new logic or it will invent status. This module has four states and says so.
Read-only-first still requires CLI execution, so this does not yet deliver the no-PowerShell owner experience.

analysis: The feedback's push decision was already executed; all five expected post-push values verified as matching, so no push action was taken or needed.

DEFECT A was not a labelling bug. The module's only derived signal is STALE; masking it defeats the module's entire reason to exist and actively routes the owner into building downstream artifacts on stale inputs.

DEFECT B contained a second, unnamed instance - the <seed-keyword> placeholder emitting bare cmd.exe redirection operators - which is more likely to be hit than the audit's own example, because it appears on a first run with no arguments.
The audit's 'zero write/exec calls' AST result is now one apparent hit via str.replace; disclosed rather than left for the re-auditor to trip over.

decisions.decision: DEFECT A and DEFECT B in separate commits
decisions.why: A is blocking, B is not. Separate commits let the re-auditor accept or revert either alone.

decisions.decision: Test committed together with its fix, not as a red commit

decisions.decision: Per-pattern newest, then minimum across patterns - not a naive min over all produced files
decisions.why: A wildcard names a set the owner keeps adding to. A naive min would mark stage 4 stale for ever over a superseded export they never deleted. Pinned by test_a_wildcard_pattern_is_satisfied_by_its_newest_match.

decisions.decision: Did not fix the pre-existing ResourceWarning
decisions.why: Out of the audited scope; every extra diff line is something the re-auditor must check.
